questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}24xy, & \,0<x<1,0<y<1-x \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(Y<X\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1-x}24xy\,\text{d}y \\  & =24x{\int }_{0}^{1-x}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =24x{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1-x} \\  & =12x(1-x)^{2}-0 \\  & =12x(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)={\begin{aligned}12x(x-1)^{2}, & \,0<x<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0<x<1,0<y<1-x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{24xy}{12x(x-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2y}{(x-1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{(x-1)^{2}}, & \,0<x<1,0<y<1-x \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<X\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}) & =P(Y<\frac{1}{3}\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\frac{1}{3})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}\frac{2y}{{(\frac{1}{3}-1)}^{2}}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}(\frac{1}{18}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}8xy, & \,0\le x\le y,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(\frac{1}{4}<X<\frac{1}{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{2}{3}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{y}8xy\,\text{d}x \\  & =8y{\int }_{0}^{y}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =8y{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{y} \\  & =4y({y}^{2}-0) \\  & =4{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)={\begin{aligned}4{y}^{3}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 1,0\le y\le x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{8xy}{4{y}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{{y}^{2}}, & \,0\le x\le y,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{4}<X<\frac{1}{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{2}{3}) & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{2}{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{2x}{{(\frac{2}{3})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{9}{4}{\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{9}{4}{[{x}^{2}]}_{1/4}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{9}{4}(\frac{3}{16}) \\  & =\frac{27}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{2y(2x+3y)}{5}, & \,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2y(2x+3y)}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{4xy}{5}+\frac{6{y}^{2}}{5})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2{x}^{2}y}{5}+\frac{6x{y}^{2}}{5}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{8y}{5}+\frac{12{y}^{2}}{5}-\frac{2y}{5}-\frac{6{y}^{2}}{5} \\  & =\frac{6{y}^{2}}{5}+\frac{6y}{5} \\  & =\frac{6y(y+1)}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{6y(y+1)}{5}, & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2y(2x+3y)}{5})}{(\frac{6y(y+1)}{5})} \\  & =\frac{2x+3y}{3(y+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3y}{3(y+1)}, & \,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
